name: mutillidae
notes:
UNVERIFIED in this build environment — no network here to pull the image or exercise the app; ports/paths/labels are from documentation and must be verified on first real launch. Canonical image: Docker Hub `citizenstig/nowasp` (OWASP Mutillidae II / "NOWASP"), a self-contained PHP app bundling Apache + PHP + MySQL in one container listening on port 80 — no separate DB container needed. (Alternative `bltsec/mutillidae-docker` is a multi-container compose stack requiring separate MySQL/LDAP services; prefer the single `citizenstig/nowasp` image for auto-launch.)

DB SETUP REQUIRED: on first run the database tables are not built. Browse to the app and click "reset/setup the DB" (the setup prompt on the home page, or visit /index.php?page=install.php / the "Setup/reset the DB" menu link) to initialize MySQL before scanning; SQLi/auth pages return errors until the schema exists. The home page `/` returns 200 even pre-setup, so it is a valid health signal, but ground-truth injection points need the DB built first. MySQL init can add startup latency — hence the 120s health timeout.

SECURITY LEVEL: Mutillidae ships at security level 0 (fully insecure) by default, so the curated points are exploitable out of the box; a UI toggle can raise it to level 5 (secured), which would suppress findings — keep it at level 0 for benchmarking.

AUTH: the five curated points are reachable unauthenticated. The `page` parameter is the classic local-file-inclusion sink (GET/QUERY_VALUE); user-info.php SQLi is a GET form (QUERY_VALUE, `username`/`password`); login.php SQLi/auth-bypass is a POST form (BODY_FORM_VALUE, `username`); dns-lookup.php is a POST form (BODY_FORM_VALUE, `target_host`) vulnerable to both OS command injection (output-reflected `nslookup`) and reflected XSS. Hence insertion_kinds includes both QUERY_VALUE and BODY_FORM_VALUE.

CURATION CAVEAT: the ground_truth labels are OUR curation (co-design), chosen as small/high-confidence/well-documented classic Mutillidae bugs — they are stable but SHOULD be independently verified against the running build; param names in particular (`page`, `username`, `target_host`) should be confirmed against the deployed version, as menu/page routing has shifted across Mutillidae releases. Deliberately vulnerable app (role=vulnerable), PHP category.
